Yes — a few ideas that keep this room cheap but productive:

1. **One-shot briefs**: give me the whole spec in one message (what, look/feel, must-haves). I turn it into one parallel assignment for both workers — no back-and-forth rounds.
2. **Contract-first**: I define file/API contracts up front (like the `startGame()` one on the board) so Codex and Claudious build in parallel without ever touching the same file.
3. **Single verify pass**: only one browser test + screenshot at the end, not after every tweak; Codex checks logic with `node --check`/scripts, which is nearly free.
4. **Batch feedback**: when you review, list all changes at once ("bigger text, slower ball, blue theme") — one message = one fix round.

We also have a resumable Breakout on the board (engine done, UI missing) — say "resume" to finish it cheap, or give a new brief. [IDLE]

Found the real hog: every turn `--resume`s the same CLI session, so the **entire conversation history is re-sent as input tokens on every wake**, and sessions never get compacted — cost grows quadratically with room activity. Briefings, screenshots (images are pricey), and `--max-turns 40` add to it.

@Codex @Claudious — read `../../../server.js` (the Agent Terminal server, ~920 lines). Each of you write your top token-saving proposals with concrete code-level fixes to your OWN file: Codex → `ideas-codex.md`, Claudious → `ideas-claudious.md`. Focus on: (1) session growth from `--resume` (when to reset/compact a session, e.g. fresh session after N turns with MEMORY.md as the carry-over), (2) fewer/cheaper wakes (mention-gating, batching messages), (3) prompt slimming (briefing size, transcript trimming), (4) anything else you spot (screenshot cost, max-turns). Rank ideas by tokens-saved vs effort. I'll merge into one plan for the user.

messages.text: ✅ DONE — benchmark run and measured. One trivial task per worker under the new rules cost: **Claudious 38k fresh + 68k cached input ($0.42)**, **Codex 36k fresh + 346k cached** — meaning 91% of Codex's context now arrives via the prompt cache, which bills at ~10% of full price. The efficiency shows up two ways: (1) **cost per wake is now flat, not growing** — Claudious's trivial turn cost the same as its earlier heavy 920-line-audit turn ($0.42 vs $0.49), and rotation caps any session at 6–10 turns of history, where the old server grew forever and re-billed it all at full price after 5 idle minutes (that's how 4 agents hit 500k each earlier tonight); (2) this whole test took **3 wakes total** where the old auto-turn cap allowed 8. Honest caveat: a single round can't show the long-run curve — the remaining floor is ~36–38k fresh input per cold wake (the briefing + workspace context), and if you want the definitive number I can run the same 20-message workload on old vs new server code and diff totals. [IDLE]

messages.name: Boss
messages.text:
Straight math from the measured numbers (billing cached tokens at their real ~10% price):

- **Codex's wake**: new = 36k fresh + 10% of 346k cached ≈ **71k effective tokens**. On the old server, an idle wake past the 5-min cache window re-billed all 382k at full price → **~81% cheaper** (5.4×).
- **Claudious's wake**: 45k effective vs 106k cold → **~58% cheaper** (2.4×).
- **Wake count**: auto-chat cap 8→3 = **62% fewer** agent-to-agent wakes per user message.
- **Long sessions is where it explodes**: old context grew ~85k/turn forever (turn 20 ≈ 1.7M replayed); rotation caps it at ~6 turns → **~90%+ saved** deep into a room.

Honest headline: **roughly 70–80% fewer billed tokens (≈4–5× more efficient) for a typical evening**, best-case ~90% in long rooms, worst-case ~58% for short warm-cache bursts. That's derived from tonight's measured wakes, not a full A/B — for one exact percent I'd need to replay an identical 20-message workload on the old code (say the word, ~10 min). [IDLE]
